title: David P. Reed
name: David P. Reed
summary: American computer scientist and network architect associated with the end-to-end argument and early internet protocol work.
whyThisMatters: Reed’s work articulated architectural principles that shaped the open internet, including where reliability and security functions belong in a networked system.

sections.overview:
David P. Reed is an American computer scientist whose work spans computer networking, distributed systems, and internet architecture. He co-authored the end-to-end argument, a highly influential account of how functions should be placed in layered communication systems.

Architectural legacy

The end-to-end argument informed the design of internet protocols and remains a reference point in debates about security, reliability, privacy, and control in networked systems. Reed’s career also included work on early network protocols and interactive computing.

timeline.event: Studies computer science at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology.
Co-authors the end-to-end argument with Jerome Saltzer and David Clark.
Works on distributed systems and network architecture.
Continues work and public writing on internet architecture.
Remains a referenced voice in discussions of network design.
